text: Owner-side review of in/hr-position-salary-access 9b7852b8 (reviewer + the brain's own reading). Result: the design is sound and migration 0124 is additive (new tables, nullable columns, checks and triggers that existing rows pass, journal one clean entry); module boundaries, admin-only position editing, ADMIN reservation, last-admin guard, salary as numeric/Decimal with run-month resolution, audit redaction, tests not weakened, mn.json 41 added keys and none changed: all fine. Three things before it can land, please put them into the same re-push as the employee-page test fix: [MEDIUM] apps/api/src/modules/hr/services/positions.service.ts assign() (about 267-330) with identity/services/staff-accounts.service.ts assignPositionRoles (about 104-115): the self guard fires only when the role set changes ('changed && userId === actor.userId'). A non-admin with hr.attendance.manage who is bound to a position can PUT their own card with another positionId whose role set is identical (or both empty) and a higher salary: nothing is refused, a next-month assignment row is written and payroll pays the other position. ADR-0243 point 3 protects access, not pay. Wanted: in assign(), a non-admin whose userId equals ctx.userId and whose requested position differs from the current one gets SELF_EDIT_FORBIDDEN; an integration test for exactly that case (same roles, different salary), and one that an ADMIN editing their own card is decided explicitly (say which and why in the ADR). [LOW] positions.service.ts save(): an ADMIN who is a member of the position they edit gets SELF_EDIT_FORBIDDEN from assignPositionRoles as soon as the role set differs and the whole save rolls back (name and salary too) with a message about 'own access'. Safe, but a sole admin bound to an admin position cannot edit it and is not told why: refuse up front with a clear problem code/text (another admin must change this position's roles) or let name/salary through when the roles are unchanged; say it in ADR-0243 and in the positions guide. [LOW] identity/services/audit-privacy.ts: payroll_* audit rows now lose before/after for every reader without hr.payroll.view and ADMIN; before, any identity.audit.read holder saw them. Correct and wanted, but ADR-0243 and docs/modules/identity.md do not say that existing payroll audit content becomes hidden: one sentence each. One business rule is with the owner now and may change point 2 of ADR-0243: on main someone without identity.users.manage cannot give roles at all; with this branch hr.attendance.manage can give any non-ADMIN position, that is its roles and its salary, to any non-admin employee, and move bound staff between positions. The brain asks the owner whether HR may do that or only ADMIN (or a new permission); do not change it until the answer is here. The brain's run of the hr/payroll/sensitive-audit/identity integration suites and the integrity suite in a copy of your head is in progress; the result follows.
